\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{भरपाई} \mr{देणे} (bharpāī deṇe)}{भरपाई देणे (bharpāī deṇe)}]{\mr{भरपाई} \mr{देणे} (bharpāī deṇe) — to compensate}

\label{lesson:MR-C549-bharpai-dene}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for to sort out, then the Marathi for to waver.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{भरपाई} \mr{देणे}}
\textbf{\mr{भरपाई} \mr{देणे}} — \emph{bharpāī deṇe} — \textquotedblleft{}to compensate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mr{विमा} \mr{कंपनीने} \mr{पुरात} \mr{बुडालेल्या} \mr{गाडीची} \mr{भरपाई} \mr{दिली}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{vimā kampanīne purāt buḍālelyā gāḍīcī bharpāī dilī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The insurance company paid for the car that sank in the flood.
\end{quote}

Past, with -\mr{ने} (he …): \mr{त्याने} \mr{भरपाई} \mr{दिली}, \emph{tyāne bharpāī dilī}.

What is lost takes -\mr{ची}: \mr{गाडीची} \mr{भरपाई} \mr{देणे}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{भरपाई} \mr{देणे}} (\emph{bharpāī deṇe}) is \mr{भरपाई}, \textquotedblleft{}making good\textquotedblright{}, built on \mr{भरणे}, \textquotedblleft{}to fill\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Sanskrit \emph{bharati} (CDIAL 9397), with \mr{देणे}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bharpāī deṇe}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bharpāī deṇe}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vimā kampanīne purāt buḍālelyā gāḍīcī bharpāī dilī.} — The insurance company paid for the car that sank in the flood.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marathi for to sort out, then the Marathi for to waver, then say \emph{bharpāī deṇe} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \mr{भरपाई} \mr{देणे} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To compensate\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{मुकणे} (mukṇe)}{मुकणे (mukṇe)}]{\mr{मुकणे} (mukṇe) — to miss out on}

\label{lesson:MR-C549-mukne}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for to waver, then the Marathi for to compensate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{मुकणे}}
\textbf{\mr{मुकणे}} — \emph{mukṇe} — \textquotedblleft{}to miss out on\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mr{आजारपणामुळे} \mr{तो} \mr{अंतिम} \mr{सामन्याला} \mr{मुकला}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ājārpaṇāmuḷe to antim sāmnyālā muklā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Because of illness he missed the final match.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \mr{तो} \mr{संधीला} \mr{मुकला}, \emph{to sandhīlā muklā}.

What is missed takes -\mr{ला}: \mr{संधीला} \mr{मुकणे}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{मुकणे}} (\emph{mukṇe}) is inherited: CDIAL lists Marathi \emph{mukṇẽ}, \textquotedblleft{}to lose\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*mukna}, \textquotedblleft{}loosed\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10157).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\label{lesson:MR-C549-kavac}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for to compensate, then the Marathi for to miss out on.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{कवच}}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{संरक्षण} (saṁrakṣaṇ)}{संरक्षण (saṁrakṣaṇ)}]{\mr{संरक्षण} (saṁrakṣaṇ) — protection}

\label{lesson:MR-C549-samraksan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for to miss out on, then the Marathi for a shield.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{संरक्षण}}
\textbf{\mr{संरक्षण}} — \emph{saṁrakṣaṇ} — \textquotedblleft{}protection\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mr{किल्ल्याच्या} \mr{संरक्षणासाठी} \mr{उंच} \mr{भिंती} \mr{होत्या}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{killyācyā saṁrakṣaṇāsāṭhī uñc bhintī hotyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There were high walls to protect the fort.
\end{quote}

Neuter.

\textbf{\mr{संरक्षण}} (\emph{saṁrakṣaṇ}) is a tatsama, taken from Sanskrit \emph{saṁrakṣaṇa}, \textquotedblleft{}guarding, protection\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{भरवसा} (bharavsā)}{भरवसा (bharavsā)}]{\mr{भरवसा} (bharavsā) — reliance; trust}

\label{lesson:MR-C549-bharavsa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for a shield, then the Marathi for protection.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{भरवसा}}
\textbf{\mr{भरवसा}} — \emph{bharavsā} — \textquotedblleft{}reliance; trust\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mr{मला} \mr{माझ्या} \mr{मित्रांवर} \mr{पूर्ण} \mr{भरवसा} \mr{आहे}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{malā mājhyā mitrāṁvar pūrṇa bharavsā āhe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I fully rely on my friends.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

The one trusted takes -\mr{वर}: \mr{मित्रांवर} \mr{भरवसा}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{भरवसा}} (\emph{bharavsā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists Marathi \emph{bharvasā}, \textquotedblleft{}confidence\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*bharavaśya}, \textquotedblleft{}dependence on support\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9398).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bharavsā}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marathi for a shield, then the Marathi for protection, then say \emph{bharavsā} again
\end{itemize}
